issues.description: The problem statement requires the end of the main loop to be marked with the label `loop_end`, but the solution uses a different label (`end_loop`) and the template does not include the `loop_end` label at all. This mismatch between the specification and the provided solution/template can confuse students about the expected label name and whether their submission matches the requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the label name consistent across artifacts. Update the solution's label from `end_loop` to `loop_end` and add the `loop_end` label at the end of the main routine in the template (after the printf/ret sequence) so the template, solution, and problem statement all refer to the same `loop_end` label.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the end of the main loop to be marked with the label `loop_end`, but the solution implementation uses `end_loop` while the template lacks any such label. This is a naming mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the loop end label) and may confuse students trying to map the requirement to the provided code and reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same label name across all artifacts. Rename the solution label `end_loop` to `loop_end` and add the `loop_end` label at the appropriate location in the template so the code matches the problem statement instruction.
